issues.display_title: Issue #1717: bug(panoramas): "Not owner" error when changing Place ID (user_id 20260)
issues.main_description_html:
Report

A user cannot change a panorama's Place ID — the request fails with a "Not owner" toast.

Affected user: user_id: 20260
Tour CID: 7068319991609668221 (tour "鷲山駅")
Sequence: #3 — file 20260724-r0024611

Steps:

  1. Open 360 Image Info at /my-tours/{mid}/edit/{pid} for that panorama.
  2. Click the pencil icon on the PlaceID row (In GoThru card).
  3. Paste a new Place ID in the Set Pano PlaceID modal, click Set.
  4. Red toast: Not owner. Place ID is not changed.

The user does own this tour — it's listed under their own My Tours.

Where it comes from

POST /panoramas/change-placeid → ChangePanoPlaceIdAction throws PanoramaNotOwnerException (PANORAMA.NOT_OWNER) when ToursRepository::checkModerationOwnership($userId, $moderationId) returns false.

Hypotheses to check, in order

A. user_id never reaches the action.
The route is registered outside the auth middleware group, so the controller reads user_id from the request body. The dashboard does not send user_id in that request — only mid, pano_id, place_id. If that's the case the check runs with 0 and fails.

→ First thing to determine: does this reproduce for every user, or only some? If it fails for everyone, this is the cause and it's a full outage of the feature, not a per-user issue.

B. The moderation row is owned by a different account.
If some users succeed, compare moderation.user_id for CID 7068319991609668221 against 20260. Likely candidates: the tour belongs to a parent/agency account and 20260 is a sub-account, or the tour was transferred between accounts.

→ If this is it, the ownership check needs to accept the parent-account relationship the same way the rest of the tour endpoints do — please check how other panorama/tour actions resolve ownership for sub-accounts and stay consistent.

Done when

  • Root cause identified and stated on this issue (A, B, or something else).
  • User 20260 can change the Place ID on that panorama.
  • Users who genuinely don't own a tour still get rejected — no loosening of the ownership check beyond the legitimate account relationship.
  • Regression check: the same flow works for a plain single-account owner.

Related

  • #1716 — moving this route into the auth group is part of that task; the two overlap, coordinate so they don't conflict.
  • GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4165 — frontend subscription gate for the same feature.

Summary of Changes — 2026-07-27

Root cause: hypothesis A. The route sat outside the auth group, so the controller read user_id from the body — which the dashboard never sends (SetPanoPlaceID.jsx:25-30 posts only mid, pano_id, place_id). ChangePanoPlaceIdDto cast the missing value to 0, so checkModerationOwnership(0, $mid) matched no row → Not owner. Broken for every user on that path, not just 20260; hypothesis B is not involved.

It looked user-specific because only the 360 Image Info pencil calls change-placeid. The Publish / Edit flows call set-placeid, which was already inside auth and worked.

Fixed as part of #1716:

  • b3f1a8b — route moved into the auth group; user_id and subscribtion now come from the token, a body-supplied user_id is shunted to client_user_id.
  • 96a4ee7 — identity read via $request->input() so an uploaded part named user_id cannot shadow the token value; adds ChangePanoPlaceIdControllerTest.

The ownership check itself is unchanged, so non-owners are still rejected.

Re-testing: a Pro/Agency gate now runs after ownership — a Basic-plan owner gets SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_ALLOWED (403), not Not owner. Body user_id is ignored, so reproducing a specific user needs that user's token.

Dev Note — After Implementation

Done in PR #1687, plus follow-up commit d09bd07.

  • Extracted to AddDataGPSController + AddDataGPSAction + AddDataGPSDto; route moved from the no-auth group into the auth group, legacy Actions/AddDataGPS.php and the ToursController method removed.
  • ToursRepository: added getBluelineModerationInfo, getPanoramaIdsForGPS, setModerationGpsFlag.
  • New domain exceptions: SubscriptionNotAllowedException (TOURS.SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_ALLOWED → 401) and BlulineOnlyException (TOURS.BLUELINE_ONLY → 409).
  • Auth move is not a breaking change: the legacy action already validated the Authorization header itself and rejected missing/expired tokens.
  • Fixed bug found while migrating: getPanoramaIdsForGPS first read the legacy helper name literally and filtered 5_pano_id IS NULL OR ''. PublishClass::getPanosInfoNoPanoId() never filtered on 5_pano_id — its real predicate is linked_moderation_id = 0 OR NULL. The wrong predicate skipped panoramas already published to Google (gps flag never set while the endpoint still returned 200) and queued panoramas linked in from another moderation. Legacy predicate restored verbatim, including the '0' string bind.
  • Also fixed: the RabbitMQ publish loop is wrapped in try/finally, so an AMQP failure mid-batch cannot leak the connection.
  • 6 unit tests, passing — subscription gate, ownership check, blueline tour-type check, LIVE happy path (payload shape, one job per panorama, monotonic timestamp), no-panoramas (gps flag must not be set), non-LIVE (gps flag set, nothing queued).
  • Docs: docs/v2/tours/misc/add-gps.md; registered as migrated API #198 in ADR_MIGRATED_APIS.md.

Summary

Panorama place_id detection during Google import runs only for a hardcoded userId whitelist; it must run for all users so nested-business place_id linkage works platform-wide.

Current state

In app/Workers/Import/PanoramaProcessor.php, processPanoramaData() gates the place_id association logic behind if (in_array($userId, [1, 2, 50214])). Outside this whitelist, $panoInfo['place_id'] is never set, so 4_panoramas.place_id falls back to the DB default (NULL) for every other user. Related user-facing report: #1770.

Target state

Every imported panorama, regardless of importing user, gets place_id populated in 4_panoramas when the photo's Google places[0].placeId differs from the tour's main place_id.

Scope

  • app/Workers/Import/PanoramaProcessor.php — processPanoramaData(), the place_id block (~line 237-241): drop the in_array($userId, ...) guard, keep the existing comparison logic ($photoPlaceId !== null && $photoPlaceId !== $placeInfo['place_id']) unconditional.

Out of scope

  • No changes to ConstellationService, moderation creation, or how many moderations get created per import (still one per CID/job).
  • No changes to PhotosService/PlaceDetailsService place lookup logic.

Risk / test plan

  • Confirm whitelisted users (1, 2, 50214) behave identically to before (no regression).

Result

Removed the in_array($userId, [1, 2, 50214]) guard in PanoramaProcessor::processPanoramaData() (app/Workers/Import/PanoramaProcessor.php:237-241). The place_id comparison logic ($photo['places'][0]['placeId'] !== $placeInfo['place_id']) now runs unconditionally for every user, so 4_panoramas.place_id gets populated on import regardless of who imports. Location

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/BuyStorageHandler.php:190-191

$invoiceData = $this->upgradeHelper->insertCCPurchaseForUpgrade(

  • name
  • pano_id
  • sub_menus

];

issues.main_description_html:
Summary

New ADR-Domain endpoint GET /v1/crm/tours/clients — batch lookup of the assigned client for many tours in one request. Consumed by ClientBadge on TourCard so the tours list needs one request per page instead of N. Design doc: docs/crm/CRM_API_DESIGN.md §4.6.

⚠️ Route registration order: register this route before GET /tours/{mid}/client so the literal clients segment is not captured by the {mid} parameter.

Request

GET /v1/crm/tours/clients?mids=12345,12346,12399
  • mids = comma-separated 0_moderation.moderation_ids, max 100 → CRM.INVALID_INPUT (400) otherwise.

Response (200)

{
  "clients": {
    "12345": { "id": 1001, "first_name": "Olivia", "...": "..." },
    "12346": null
  },
  "messages": "Data retrieved"
}

SQL

SELECT m.moderation_id, c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name, c.company, c.email, c.phone
FROM 0_moderation m
LEFT JOIN crm_clients c ON c.id = m.crm_client_id
WHERE m.moderation_id IN (:mids) AND m.user_id = :user_id;

Requirements

  • Idempotent per item: missing/not-owned mids map to null (no per-item error).
  • Owner-scoped by user_id (auth middleware).
  • SQL isolated in CrmRepository.

  • Unknown/not-owned mids → null (no 404 per item)
  • Route order verified (not shadowed by {mid} route)

issues.main_description_html:
Context & Problem

During the 60-day payment failure audit (Issue #2023), an incident occurred on 2026-10-02 where User 2426 (picasa_tokyo1@datadisk.jp) unlocked stitching for tour TENyOPaW (moderation 3588134).

The sequence of events was:

  1. The customer's credit card was successfully charged $25.50 USD by Stripe (ch_3UM0r54UXotNjjkI1q1v4173).
  2. The database transaction committed successfully (is_stich_payed = 1, and unlocked_cid_stich record was created).
  3. Immediately after database persistence, UnlockStitchingHelpers::processUnlockStitchingSuccess() invoked prepareInvoiceData() synchronously.
  4. An unhandled exception was thrown during PDF generation (Dompdf font cache permission error on storage/fonts/installed-fonts.json).
  5. Because prepareInvoiceData() was outside exception isolation, the unhandled error propagated up to the controller, returning an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error response to the user's browser.
  6. The user, believing the payment failed, resubmitted payment 13 minutes later, resulting in an inadvertent duplicate charge ($25.50 + $25.50).

In one-time payments, the primary financial contract (card charge + access provisioning in DB) must not be aborted or reported as a failure due to secondary receipt generation errors.

Scope of Work

  1. Non-Blocking Invoice Generation:
    • Wrap $this->invoiceHelper->prepareInvoiceData() in UnlockStitchingHelpers::processUnlockStitchingSuccess() within a non-blocking try...catch (\Throwable $e) block.
    • Log any PDF generation errors to application logs with context (user_id, transaction_id, moderation_id) without interrupting the success flow.
    • Allow the transaction to return HTTP 200 OK and trigger access confirmation even if the PDF fails to render on disk.
  2. Graceful Email Delivery:
    • Ensure receipt email payload gracefully handles absent or null $invoiceData (invoice_url empty string) without throwing errors.
    • Wrap customer and support email notifications in error isolation so email transport glitches do not fail the HTTP response.
  3. Automated Unit Testing:
    • Add unit tests verifying that when prepareInvoiceData() throws an exception, processUnlockStitchingSuccess() still successfully completes and returns HTTP 200.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Successful Stripe charge and database persistence always returns HTTP 200 OK, even if PDF invoice generation fails.
  • PDF rendering exceptions are caught, logged, and do not trigger charge failure handlers or misleading HTTP 500 responses.
  • Email delivery handles missing invoice URL gracefully.
  • Unit tests pass with 100% pass rate.

issues.main_description_html:
Description

Backend changes have been implemented to allow Google Stats and TourMkr stats to be accessible via custom whitelabel domains. Each whitelabel account has it's own domain.

the rule is:

  • https://gstats.co/stats_b3c5a32690225492598b809b4df92b92 -> https://www.virtuo-reality.com/stats-b3c5a32690225492598b809b4df92b92

API

GET /portfolios/gstats?cid=128158523644165989

We now need to update the frontend UI so that the buttons directing users to these stats use their configured whitelabel domain instead of the default application domain. This UI change must be conditionally applied based on the user's subscription tier and domain settings.

Business Logic & Conditions

The link replacement logic should ONLY trigger if the user meets both of the following criteria:

  1. Subscription Tier: The account is currently on the Agency OR Yearly Agency plan.
  2. Configuration: The account has a valid whitelabel domain set up.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. For Agency/Yearly Agency accounts WITH a whitelabel domain: Clicking "Tour Stats" or "Google Stats" successfully redirects the user to the stats page hosted on their specific whitelabel domain.
  2. For all other accounts (or Agency accounts without a whitelabel domain setup): Clicking those same buttons redirects the user to the standard, default stats URL.
  3. The UI rendering and link replacement do not cause noticeable delays or layout shifts on the My Tours or Virtual Tour Manager pages.
